usage: The phrase means having a very positive or successful beginning, especially at the start of a new venture or project.
It is commonly used in contexts related to business, career, or any undertaking where initial success is emphasized.
You can use it to encourage someone or to describe a fortunate event that sets a good tone for the future.
It often implies not just a good start, but one that brings benefits or profits right away.
This expression is formal enough to appear in speeches or writing, yet it is also used in casual conversation.

examples.sentence: 新年做生意，真係希望有個開門紅利。
examples.jyutping: san1 nin4 zou6 sang1 ji3, zan1 hai6 hei1 mong6 jau5 go3 hoi1 mun4 hung4 lei6.
examples.meaning: At the start of the new year business, I really hope to have a great start.

examples.sentence: 佢喺新公司做得幾好，真係開門紅利。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 hai2 san1 gung1 si1 zou6 dak1 gei2 hou2, zan1 hai6 hoi1 mun4 hung4 lei6.
examples.meaning: He did quite well at the new company, truly a great start.

examples.sentence: 開門紅利代表住未來有好嘅發展機會。
examples.jyutping: hoi1 mun4 hung4 lei6 doi6 biu2 zyu6 mei6 loi4 jau5 hou2 ge3 faat3 zin2 gei1 wui6.
examples.meaning: A great start represents good opportunities for development in the future.

examples.sentence: 聽講你哋開幕禮好成功，真係開門紅利呀！
examples.jyutping: teng1 gong2 nei5 dei6 hoi1 muk6 lai5 hou2 sing4 gung1, zan1 hai6 hoi1 mun4 hung4 lei6 aa3!
examples.meaning: I heard your opening ceremony was very successful, truly a great start!
